policy_title: Reform property taxes towards a Land Value Tax
stated: Work towards a long-term policy of Land Value Tax, re-evaluate Council Tax bands to reflect current values, and remove business rate relief on Enterprise Zones, Freeports, petrol stations, and most empty properties. Conduct a survey of all landholdings.

source.quote: Our long-term policy aim is a Land Value Tax so that those with the most valuable and largest land holdings would contribute the most. In the next parliament, elected Greens will take steps towards this by pushing for: • Re-evaluation of Council Tax bands to reflect big changes in value since 1990s. • Removal of business rate relief on Enterprise Zones, Freeports, petrol stations and most empty properties. • A survey of all landholdings to pave the way for fair taxation of land.

bearing_set.reason: LVT structurally incentivises development over land-banking and holding idle land, removing empty-property rate relief pressures owners to use or sell, and the land survey targets concentration — all directly bearing on housing supply and affordability.

Re-evaluating Council Tax bands to current values directly changes millions of households' bills (a core cost-of-living expense), potentially substantially redistributing the burden between lower- and higher-value homes.

Council Tax band revaluation shifts the tax burden between households (likely upward for many, since 1991 valuations are outdated); LVT reform changes the incidence of property taxation from transactions to annual land value; removing business rate reliefs raises the tax burden on affected commercial occupiers — all are direct take-home/tax-burden effects.

Removing business rate reliefs across Enterprise Zones, Freeports, petrol stations and most empty properties is a concrete revenue-raising measure with a direct, quantifiable effect on the funded/borrowed balance.

Removing investment-incentive reliefs in Enterprise Zones and Freeports reduces site-specific business formation and investment incentives (concrete mechanism: reduced return on marginal investment in those zones); the offsetting LVT efficiency gain (less distortionary than labour/transaction taxes, per Mirrlees Review) could improve allocative productivity — the net effect on aggregate living standards and business dynamism is genuinely contested.

LVT incidence falls on landowners, who are disproportionately concentrated among the wealthier; Council Tax revaluation reduces the current regressivity of the 1991-band system — both shift the distribution of tax burden in a direction that narrows the rich-poor gap through the taxation of land rents.

membership_note: Five fundamentals clear the non-negligible bar: the policy is a package that simultaneously reshapes housing market incentives (O1), redistributes household and business tax burdens (O11, O14), raises public revenue (O12), and affects investment patterns and economic efficiency in ways economists actively contest (O13).
